champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
ordered_diagnoses: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and muscle weakness with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin
salient_findings: Mild weakness in bilateral hip flexor muscles
Elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase) and bilirubin
key_facts: 71-year-old man presented with three weeks of jaundice
Weight loss and abdominal pain reported
Bilateral lower-extremity weakness, most noticeable when arising from a chair
No history of autoimmune or neuromuscular conditions
Taking atorvastatin as a home medication
Epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound on physical examination
Significant elevation in creatinine kinase (CK) level
CT abdomen/pelvis showed a 2.6 × 3.1 cm pancreatic head mass
MRI showed diffuse myositis affecting lower extremities
Pancreatic head biopsy was hypocellular with scant atypical cells
Biliary stricture biopsy was consistent with adenocarcinoma

raw.champion: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain, and a pancreatic head mass is consistent with pancreatic cancer. The significant elevation in creatinine kinase level and MRI findings of diffuse myositis suggest a paraneoplastic syndrome, specifically necrotizing myopathy, which is a known complication of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
